reason: Every other module speaks this vocabulary. The ElevenLabs agent is configured against these exact field names, so they are a frozen external contract rather than an internal convenience.
description: Pydantic request/response models for all six HTTP endpoints plus the internal session and event records. Field names match the ElevenLabs agent tool configuration exactly and must not be renamed.

reason: The orchestrator holds applicant PII and is reachable from the public internet so the voice agent can call it. An unauthenticated write path would let anyone inject field values into a live session.
description: FastAPI dependency that verifies the X-Zuzu-Secret header against ZUZU_SHARED_SECRET using a constant-time comparison, rejecting missing or wrong secrets with 401.

reason: This file is the product thesis: a form is data, not code. Adding a new USCIS form must mean adding a schema, not writing a new module.
description: Loader and validator for the declarative I-765 field schema in data/i765_form_schema.json, whose entries carry the field id, plain-language spoken question, value type, sensitivity flag, mapping group, memory key, and the exact AcroForm field name(s) it fills.

reason: Keeps the routes form-agnostic so a second form is a registry entry rather than a branch in the request handler.
description: Drop-in registry mapping a form_id such as I-765 to its schema, with lookup and listing helpers that raise a clear error for unknown forms.

reason: Session state must live behind an interface from day one. Layer 2 swaps in Redis for horizontal scale, and that has to be a config flip rather than a rewrite of every call site.
description: SessionStore protocol plus an in-memory implementation. Tracks per-session collected values with provenance and answers which schema fields are still missing.

reason: The dashboard's live-fill effect is the demo's visual payload, and it must not add latency to the voice path. Publishing is fire-and-forget behind an interface that Redis pub/sub replaces in Layer 2.
description: EventBus protocol plus an in-memory asyncio implementation. Publishes per-session events and lets the WebSocket endpoint subscribe to a single session's stream.

reason: The completed PDF is the deliverable the applicant actually files. This form is encrypted, carries a stale XFA overlay that blanks the page in Acrobat, and uses irregular per-field checkbox export values -- a naive fill silently produces an empty form.
description: Fills the official I-765 AcroForm from collected session values and writes a completed PDF, handling decryption, XFA removal, checkbox export values, and appearance generation.

reason: The single process the ElevenLabs widget talks to. Read and write paths must stay in the tens of milliseconds because a human is waiting mid-sentence.
description: FastAPI application exposing the six contract endpoints, the per-session WebSocket stream, the Demo Mode trigger, and a health check.

reason: Decouples building the orchestrator from owning the voice agent, and doubles as the Demo Mode fallback so the demo survives a dead microphone or a flaky conference network.
description: Scripted client that drives a full call through the public HTTP contract exactly as the ElevenLabs agent would, from session init to a generated PDF.
